name: Idealising a scalar fault gadget
summary: The noisy edge of a disconnected fault gadget can be made fault-free: a fault without observable effect can be ignored.
description:
A fault gadget that has no targets is a scalar diagram: a red and a green one-legged spider connected by an edge. On the left-hand side this edge is noisy, with weight vector $\vec w$ (weights of its $X$-, $Y$- and $Z$-flips); on the right-hand side it is fault-free. A flip on it only changes a global scalar, so it has no observable effect, and the two sides are fault-equivalent.

Semantically the two sides are the same ZX-diagram; only the noise annotation changes. As in the paper, noisy edges are labelled with their weight (the cost of a flip on that edge; a vector of weights for the $X$-, $Y$- and $Z$-flips, unlabelled noisy edges have weight 1), and *fault-free* (idealised) edges are drawn bold purple. These annotations are shown on the rule as stated; derived variants (transpose, colour swap, other legs counts) may drop them.
